A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same AutoComPose research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, revised and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments and ablations on FIXMYPOSE, PoseFixCPR and AIST-CPR in Tables 1–5, with additional qualitative results in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline controls, a Stage I ablation and a GPT-4o mini experiment in Tables 6–7.

M1.justification: Equations (1)–(2) correct the stated classification and cycle losses from log(-p) to -log(p). The generation stages, architecture, original prompts and loss weighting remain unchanged. This establishes a correction to documented objectives, not an implementation change or retraining.

E1.justification: Both versions use FIXMYPOSE, PoseFixCPR and AIST-CPR for the same composed pose retrieval tasks. The added studies use existing datasets; alternative prompts and GPT-4o mini change configurations rather than data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds an evaluated rule-based comparator augmented with cyclic training. It also includes paraphrased human descriptions. The original human-annotation, rule-based, CLIP and Combiner comparisons in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New CLIP-RN50 experiments vary baseline paraphrase counts and cyclic training on PoseFixCPR, and test removal of body-part prompting or substitution of GPT-4o mini on FIXMYPOSE. Existing splits, gallery sizes, retrieval metrics and training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 6–7 add targeted analyses of whether paraphrasing and cyclic training benefit competing annotations, whether Stage I helps, and whether a smaller MLLM remains effective. These additions are confined to CLIP-RN50 settings; the existing augmentation, cyclic-loss, paraphrasing and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and the qualitative retrieval examples are unchanged. Table 6 adds PoseFixCPR R@1 results of 52.02 for paraphrased human annotations and 55.05 for rule-based annotations with cyclic training. Table 7 adds FIXMYPOSE R@1 values of 8.63 without Stage I and 6.67 with GPT-4o mini. These are additional configurations, not revised original scores.

T1.justification: The correction from log(-p) to -log(p) in Equations (1)–(2) repairs loss definitions that otherwise take logarithms of negative probabilities. Other mathematical definitions and assumptions remain unchanged, and no proofs or theorems are added.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same framework, benchmark, annotation-efficiency and retrieval-performance claims. The contribution list is condensed and reordered; broad applicability remains asserted in the conclusion despite losing its separate bullet.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the explanation based on precise 3D pair selection and real-world complexity with gallery size, pose diversity and retrieval ambiguity. New discussion extends cyclic training's applicability to rule-based annotations and supports smaller MLLMs. Appendix A calls Stage I critical despite Table 7 showing higher R@1 without it and only small decreases in other recalls.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 identifier, modified ablation prompts in Figures 15–16, and sources for baseline paraphrases and reverse descriptions. It newly quantifies rejected generation responses as fewer than 2.5%. Existing hardware, training hyperparameters and original prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v2 removes Chu et al. (2017) and Rogez and Schmid (2016), together with their associated sentence about holistic descriptions. It also fixes the AIST++ citation to the already cited Li et al. work. The broader CPR, CIR and MLLM research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction and contribution list receive localized condensation and rewriting. The appendix separates Additional Results from Dataset Details, moving the former prompt section from B to C. Most prose, including the abstract and conclusion, is retained.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 revise labels and the augmentation illustration; Tables 6–7 and prompt Figures 15–16 are added. Existing qualitative and dataset images remain, with the word-cloud and example-pair figures reordered and relocated. The overall two-column design is preserved.

improvement.justification: The added baseline controls, smaller-model experiment, explicit ablation prompts and corrected loss formulas make v2 more informative and reproducible while preserving the original results. The benefit is limited: the new experiments use one backbone, and the claimed critical importance of Stage I exceeds the small, mixed effects in Table 7 without uncertainty estimates.
